hero.title: Empower Farmers South Sudan (EFSS)
hero.subtitle: Building food-secure and climate-resilient communities across South Sudan.

glance.heading: EFSS At a Glance
glance.intro: Empowering farmers. Equipping youth. Restoring land.

mission.heading: Our Mission
mission.intro: Helping farmers grow more food with less effort
mission.text1: Empower Farmers South Sudan (EFSS) is the conservation agriculture programme of EmpowerKids–South Sudan. EFSS teaches smallholder farmers how to grow more food with less effort through the Foundations for Farming model.
mission.text2: Our mission is to improve food security, create dignified agricultural livelihoods for communities, restore degraded land and help farming households become more resilient to climate and economic pressures.
mission.text3: We believe that practical knowledge, disciplined farming practices and locally trained leaders can help communities build stronger and more productive agricultural systems.

challenge.heading: The Challenge
challenge.intro: Food insecurity. Degraded soils. Uncertain harvests.
challenge.text: Food insecurity and soil degradation threaten millions of families in South Sudan. Years of conflict, climate shocks and unsustainable farming practices have left soils exhausted and harvests unreliable. Many smallholder farmers work hard but still face:
challenge.conclusion: EFSS exists to help turn that hard work into stronger harvests, healthier soils and more stable livelihoods.

strategy.heading: Our Strategy
strategy.intro: Three pathways to stronger farms and stronger communities

items.title: Train Farmers Where They Are
items.subtitle: Practical learning in real farming environments
items.description: EFSS delivers training directly within farmers' own communities and fields rather than in distant classrooms. Using household Pfumvudza plots, village demonstration sites, schools and churches as training venues, farmers learn conservation agriculture in their real production environments.
bullets: Removes barriers of distance and cost
Allows farmers to apply skills immediately

items.title: Equip Youth to Lead
items.subtitle: Building the next generation of agricultural leaders
items.description: EFSS places youth at the centre of agricultural transformation. Young people are trained and mentored as Interns, Fellows, and Champions. Through structured Train-the-Trainer courses, field supervision and leadership development, young people gain the technical, facilitation and ethical skills required to serve as community agriculture leaders.

items.title: Restore Land and Grow Markets
items.subtitle: Moving households from survival toward surplus
items.description: EFSS combines soil restoration with market-focused farming. Through composting, mulching, agroforestry, moisture conservation, soil restoration, farmer organisation, collective marketing and buyer linkages, degraded land can be rehabilitated and productivity restored.

principles.title: With Joy
principles.description: Agriculture is approached with commitment, dignity, discipline and a positive attitude.

pfumvudza.heading: Pfumvudza
pfumvudza.intro: A precision-based household food security system
pfumvudza.text: Pfumvudza is a precision-based household farming system designed to enable a family of six to produce sufficient, high-quality staple food for one year from a small, well-managed plot. The system uses permanent planting basins, early planting, mulching, strict agronomic discipline, precise spacing and careful crop management.

demonstrationFarming.heading: Demonstration Farming
demonstrationFarming.text: EFSS operates Pfumvudza demonstration farms as the foundation of its training and quality assurance system. These sites function as living classrooms where smallholder farmers, youth leaders, schools and partners can observe and practise conservation agriculture in real field conditions.

whatWeDo.title: Establish standard plots
whatWeDo.description: Establish standard 16m × 39m Pfumvudza plots as household food security units.

whatWeDo.title: Demonstrate correct practices
whatWeDo.description: Show farmers correct spacing, planting depth, compost application, mulching, thinning and crop management.

whatWeDo.title: Host field learning
whatWeDo.description: Host seasonal field days, farmer open days and institutional trainings.

whatWeDo.title: Quality control
whatWeDo.description: Use demonstration farms as quality-control hubs before scaling training into communities.

demonstrationFarming.whyItMatters: Demonstration farms ensure that EFSS training moves beyond theory. Farmers can see visible results, including improved soil condition, stronger crop stands, better crop management and higher yields. This builds confidence and accelerates adoption of Conservation Agriculture – Foundations for Farming (CA-FfF) practices.

impact.heading: Our Impact
impact.intro: Behind every number is a family taking a step toward food security
impact.fromPilotToScale: Launched in 2025 as a pilot, the Empower Farmers South Sudan Programme is now building momentum for nationwide expansion in 2026. The goal is to move from demonstration and training into broader community adoption, creating a scalable system of trained farmers and youth agricultural leaders across South Sudan.

trainTheTrainer.heading: Train-the-Trainer

trainTheTrainer.text: The EFSS Train-the-Trainer (ToT) Programme professionalises youth as conservation agriculture instructors and community resource persons.

whatWeDo.description: Training young leaders in Foundations for Farming methodology.

whatWeDo.description: Delivering structured two-day Train-the-Trainer courses with optional field practicum extensions.

whatWeDo.title: Build facilitation skills
whatWeDo.description: Developing the communication and teaching abilities needed to train other farmers.

whatWeDo.title: Ethics & safeguarding
whatWeDo.description: Providing ethics orientation, safeguarding standards and assessment.

whatWeDo.title: Professional ToT services

trainTheTrainer.whyItMatters: By equipping youth with technical and leadership skills, EFSS creates a sustainable training system that can continue beyond individual programme cycles. The approach also creates a pathway for national replication of conservation agriculture.

whatWeDo.description: Follow up with farmers after training to support correct implementation.

nationalAdoption.whyItMatters: The campaign is designed to help make Conservation Agriculture – Foundations for Farming (CA-FfF) a community-owned movement. The goal is to embed conservation agriculture within everyday farming systems and local institutions.

agroforestry.heading: Agroforestry & Climate Change
agroforestry.text: EFSS integrates agroforestry and climate-smart practices throughout its conservation agriculture model to respond to climate change and environmental degradation.

whatWeDo.title: Restore soil
whatWeDo.description: Promote compost-based soil restoration and permanent soil cover through mulching.

whatWeDo.title: Plant trees
whatWeDo.description: Integrate tree planting and agroforestry into Pfumvudza systems.

whatWeDo.title: Conserve moisture
whatWeDo.description: Train farmers in moisture conservation and minimum tillage.

whatWeDo.title: Diversify production
whatWeDo.description: Promote crop diversification to strengthen resilience.

whatWeDo.title: Establish nurseries
whatWeDo.description: Develop demonstration tree nurseries and household woodlots.

agroforestry.whyItMatters: These practices help rebuild soil fertility, reduce vulnerability to drought, respond to erratic rainfall, protect smallholder livelihoods, improve long-term land productivity and support more resilient farming communities. The goal is to ensure that future generations inherit productive and resilient farmland.
